title: Uber puts all 30,000 employees on ChatGPT Work
content:
Uber and OpenAI announced an expansion of their partnership on Thursday, with the ride-share giant telling TechCrunch that its entire global workforce — some 30,000 people — will now be using ChatGPT Work.
ChatGPT Work was introduced in July as an enterprise-focused AI agent that corporate teams could deploy for various workflows.
Uber originally piloted ChatGPT Work with 1,000 employees earlier this year but has now scaled up its usage to the entire company.
That earlier pilot was deployed to workers from across Uber’s various departments, including finance, operations, and product. Indeed, a majority of the early adopters — some 80% — were non-engineers, Sumanth Sukumar, Uber’s VP of engineering, told TechCrunch.
“They used it for a wide range of tasks: analyzing complex data from our operations to identify trends and develop recommendations; localizing training materials for different markets and languages; and building personalized interactive dashboards to manage their daily work,” he said.
Yet while the ride-share giant is now going all in on ChatGPT, it has not settled on exactly how employees will use it. “Our approach is to make powerful AI tools available across Uber while giving teams room to experiment,” Sukumar said. “For example, earlier this year we paired 30 AI engineers with teams across Uber and gave them two weeks to automate key parts of their job. Those ‘AI pods’ showed us how much opportunity there is when you combine technical expertise with a deep understanding of a particular job.”
Uber didn’t disclose how much it’s spending on the new rollout of the chatbot. Instead, Sukumar said the company will track how employees use the tool. “We’ll look at how employees are using the technology, the kinds of workflows they develop and how it helps them work more effectively. We’ll evaluate those outcomes and use what we learn to guide how we deploy AI across the business,” he said. Uber says OpenAI worked closely with the company on integrating the chatbot.
OpenAI has moved quickly to scale up its enterprise business as it competes with its chief competitor, Anthropic. Once known largely as a consumer brand, the ChatGPT creator has swiftly gained a loyal following with business customers, while other AI companies have struggled to keep up.

report.summary: Uber expands its OpenAI partnership, rolling out ChatGPT Work to all 30,000 employees after a 1,000-person pilot, marking a major enterprise AI deployment.
report.background: Uber’s move reflects a broader shift in enterprise AI from experimentation to company-wide deployment. ChatGPT Work, launched in July, is an enterprise-focused agent designed for team workflows rather than individual chat. OpenAI is racing to grow its business customer base and compete with Anthropic, which has strong enterprise traction. Uber’s earlier pilot involved 1,000 workers across finance, operations, and product, with 80% non-engineers—a signal that generative AI is moving beyond software teams. Uber also tested AI pods, pairing engineers with business teams to automate tasks. The company has not disclosed spending, emphasizing experimentation and outcome tracking instead. The rollout shows large firms are willing to buy AI seats at scale, but still need to discover which workflows deliver returns.
key_points: Uber is making ChatGPT Work available to its entire global workforce of about 30,000 people, scaling up from an earlier 1,000-employee pilot. The company did not disclose spending and says it will track usage, workflows, and outcomes to guide future AI deployment.

The pilot showed adoption was not limited to engineers: about 80% of early users came from finance, operations, and product. They used ChatGPT Work for complex operational data analysis, localizing training materials across markets and languages, and building personalized dashboards for daily work.

Uber is avoiding a top-down mandate on exactly how teams use the tool. Instead, it is giving teams room to experiment, including 'AI pods' that paired 30 AI engineers with business teams for two weeks to automate key parts of their jobs.

The expansion deepens Uber’s partnership with OpenAI and comes as OpenAI pushes aggressively into enterprise sales against Anthropic. ChatGPT Work, launched in July, is positioned as an enterprise AI agent for corporate workflows, not just a consumer chatbot.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Uber’s company-wide rollout is a strong validation of enterprise agents and seat-based AI deployment, especially among non-engineers. It signals that large enterprises will buy AI at scale, but also that value depends on workflow redesign, training, and measurement. For developers, the opportunity shifts toward integrations, observability, security, and automation tooling that make AI agents reliable inside complex organizations. For regular users, expect AI assistants to become a standard workplace utility, with productivity gains balanced by oversight, data privacy, and job-redesign concerns. The rollout also intensifies competition between OpenAI and Anthropic for enterprise accounts, likely accelerating features around admin controls, compliance, and team collaboration.
report.tools: Watch OpenAI’s ChatGPT Work and Anthropic’s Claude for Enterprise as leading enterprise-agent offerings. For implementation, compare Microsoft Copilot and Google Gemini for Workspace; use n8n or Zapier for workflow automation; and LangSmith or LangFuse for agent observability and evaluation. These tools help teams move from ad hoc chatbot use to governed, measurable AI workflows.
